slots.label: Heading 1
slots.default: The symptom is that you only think about IT when it breaks

slots.label: Paragraph 1
slots.default: If technology only reaches the agenda when something has gone wrong, then every decision gets made under pressure and usually costs more than it needed to.

slots.label: List item 1
slots.default: A refresh plan for hardware before it fails

slots.label: List item 2
slots.default: A renewal calendar with dates and costs

slots.label: List item 3
slots.default: Somewhere to see risks written down

slots.label: List item 4
slots.default: A budget line for IT rather than surprises

slots.label: List item 5
slots.default: A view of what growth will require

slots.label: List item 6
slots.default: Evidence ready for client security questionnaires

slots.label: Paragraph 3
slots.default: A server fails and suddenly there is an unbudgeted five figure decision to make in a fortnight. A renewal lands that nobody knew was coming, on terms nobody negotiated. Laptops get replaced one at a time as they die, which is the most expensive way to do it. Somebody asks whether you are secure enough for a new client’s questionnaire and the answer is a shrug.

slots.label: Heading 3
slots.default: It is not a technology failure

slots.label: Paragraph 4
slots.default: It is the absence of a plan, and it is entirely fixable. The point of strategy work is not a document that impresses people. It is knowing what is coming, roughly what it costs and roughly when, so decisions get made deliberately with time to shop around.
